title: Guardian Brief: Mini Workshop for Dedicated Capacity Controls
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design exploration and prototype for a compact 'Guardian' briefing panel inside the Redwood Console that surfaces GPU pool health, autoscaling controls, and a lightweight burst composer for on-call operators and platform teams. The goal is to provide high-signal telemetry + safe control affordances in a single, copyable UI surface that fits into the existing cluster detail page and can be used as a snapshot in Rollouts and Incident cards.
acceptance_criteria: Guardian panel implemented as a collapsible strip on cluster detail page
Key metrics displayed: cpu/gpu utilization, queue depth, avg latency P50/P95, estimated cost burn rate
Burst composer modal allows operator to request temporary capacity with explicit duration, cost estimate, and rollback hysteresis
Autoscale controls expose min/max pool size, target utilization, and hysteresis window with clear defaults
Design prototype reviewed and signed off by Eng + PM; accessible color contrast and keyboard interactions validated
design_notes: Information architecture: prioritize live health indicators and immediate guardrail actions. Primary row shows pool health (status pill), estimated headroom, and active bursts.
Guardian strip components: left-side compact sparkline for 1h/24h utilization, middle chip group for key metrics, right-side action set (Autoscale Quick, Burst, View History)
Burst composer flow: 3-step modal (reason & duration -> cost preview & SLO impact -> confirm + suggested rollback policy). Include 'simulate' mode to preview effect on SLOs without changing capacity.
Autoscale controls: inline editable min/max + target util slider. Add 'suggested profile' button driven by Optimize heuristics (server-supplied).
SLO overlays: option to overlay latency SLO lines on utilization charts and show estimated breach probability when changing controls.
Cost anchoring: show incremental cost delta and % change vs baseline for requested burst or autoscale change. Default to show 24h projected spend impact.
Density tradeoff: create a compact collapsed version for teams with many pools; expand on hover or click to reveal full composer and history timeline.
Accessibility: focus states for composer controls, ARIA labels for metric chips, color palettes checked for WCAG AA contrast against background.
Responsive behavior: guardian strip collapses to stacked rows below 800px width; composer uses full-screen modal on narrow viewports.
Telemetry hooks: design includes spots for 'why' tooltips that link to the Console cost breakdown and model inference traces (for capacity-related latencies).
decisions: Use a single compact strip on cluster detail page rather than a full separate dashboard to reduce navigation overhead
Burst requests require explicit duration and cost preview; auto-approval is not permitted—default to 'request' -> goes to operator flow unless owner-internal flag is set
Autoscale target will be expressed as target utilization percentage (vs absolute replicas) to make it hardware-agnostic
Default hysteresis window will be 5 minutes with a UI control to expand to 1/5/15/60 minutes
Prototype will be implemented with mocked Optimize suggestions; final suggestions require backend support from ENG-60012
tradeoffs: High information density vs cognitive load: we compress key signals into chips and sparklines to keep the strip compact, accepting some loss of deep historical context (link to full telemetry dashboard for deep dive).
Immediate control vs guardrails: enabling 'Quick Burst' improves ops velocity but increases risk. Mitigation: require explicit cost preview and a rollback policy default.
Suggested profiles vs user control: offering Optimize-backed suggestions reduces decision friction but requires trust; the UI surfaces source and confidence of suggestions to increase transparency.
next_steps: Finalize Figma frames for collapsed/expanded strip and burst composer (iterations 1.1 -> 1.3)
Handoff tokens and micro-interaction spec to frontend: animations for expand/collapse, confirmation toast, and error states
Schedule cross-discipline review with ENG (runtime & backend), PM, and Security to validate APIs needed for cost previews (ENG-60012) and RBAC checks
Create engineering ticket(s) for API mocks and UI integration tests (eng ticket placeholders in dependencies)
Run a short hallway usability test with two platform engineers and one customer success rep and incorporate feedback
